usage: This is the standard, everyday way to apologize for a mistake or express regret. The word is an active participle, so it must match the gender of the speaker (aasef for a man, aasefeh for a woman). For a deeper or more formal apology, Levantine speakers frequently use 'b3etezer' (I apologize).

variants.label: female speaker
variants.note: Used when the person apologizing is a woman.

variants.label: more formal
variants.note: Used for a more sincere apology or in slightly more formal situations.

variants.label: asking forgiveness (to a man)
variants.note: Used to directly ask a male listener to forgive you.

variants.label: asking forgiveness (to a woman)
variants.note: Used to directly ask a female listener to forgive you.

variants.label: plural speaker
variants.note: Used when apologizing on behalf of a group or as a couple.

responses.english: Don't worry about it (to a man)

examples.english: I'm sorry, I didn't mean it.
I'm sorry I'm late (female speaker to a man).
